diagnoses.description: When allowing special sentinel/terminal nodes, either (a) exclude them from reachability requirements, or (b) ensure they are included in the traversal model used by validators (e.g., as an explicit node reachable via explicit edges). Mismatches cause false 'unreachable' failures even when edges refer to the sentinel.
diagnoses.evidence: Verifier failure: `AssertionError: Unreachable nodes found: ['End']...` and verifier BFS explicitly skips enqueueing `tgt == 'End'` while computing reachability. Trajectory shows generated JSON includes node `{'id': 'End', ...}` and edges referencing `-> End` exist in script (grep shows lines 725/728). Therefore 'End' will never be marked reachable by the verifier's algorithm, making it unreachable by construction if included as a node.

diagnoses.description: When a skill package provides canonical builders/validators/serializers, bypassing them often leads to subtle schema/logic mismatches (sentinel handling, node typing rules, visualization conventions).
diagnoses.evidence: Run metadata: `n_skill_invocations: 0` despite skill being preloaded. The implemented solution writes JSON/DOT manually (seen in trajectory: custom parse_script building lists/dicts; custom dot printing). Only failure is a semantic edge case (End reachability) that a canonical validator might have handled or documented.

diagnoses.description: When period search returns a strong candidate, the highest peak can correspond to an alias (half/double period) due to sampling, transit shape symmetry, or detrending artifacts. A robust workflow must explicitly test harmonics (P/2, 2P) and select based on physical/diagnostic consistency (odd-even, transit count consistency, phase-fold shape), not just maximum power.

locations.section: Common Issues and Solutions / Issue: Period is 2x or 0.5x expected

diagnoses.evidence: Verifier expected 5.35699 d but output was 1.39825 d. In-run evidence shows multiple strong candidates: TLS broad best at 2.798475 d (SDE~6.54) and also peaks near 1.394978 d; BLS global best at ~1.39823 d with 2P~2.79862 d having lower but still substantial power. The run explicitly computed half/double neighborhoods yet did not use them to override the final choice.

diagnoses.description: Flattening/detrending choices (window length, polynomial order, break handling) can distort transit shapes and relative depths, amplifying aliases or suppressing the true period. A workflow should select detrending parameters based on cadence, expected transit duration, and stellar variability timescale, and confirm that candidate periods are stable across reasonable detrending settings.

locations.section: Removing Long-Term Trends / Flattening with Lightkurve

diagnoses.evidence: Run shows flatten window_length sweeps and that BLS period near 1.398 d is extremely stable across window lengths (1201–3001), while TLS reported a longer duration (~0.3086 d) and BLS refinement often maxed at duration=0.45 d (upper bound). This suggests duration grid and detrending may be absorbing variability and favoring certain periods; no stability test comparing candidate periods (including longer-period possibilities like 5.35699 d) across detrending was performed.

diagnoses.description: Period searches must set bounds informed by observation baseline and expected planet periods. If the true period is near a significant fraction of the baseline, missing or underweighting that region can yield spurious shorter-period detections. Workflows should set period_min/max and resolution based on baseline, and verify that multiple transits are expected/observed.
diagnoses.evidence: Data baseline printed as ~25.43 days. Output period was 1.398 d; verifier expected 5.35699 d (still within 15 d, so not excluded), but the workflow did not explicitly ensure candidates correspond to plausible transit counts and did not present transit_count-based gating before writeback.

diagnoses.description: When a task provides a skill bundle, the agent proceeds with ad-hoc implementation without explicitly applying any skill guidance, increasing risk of convention drift, missed requirements, and unnecessary complexity.
diagnoses.evidence: Run metadata shows `n_skill_invocations: 0` with six preloaded skills; task explicitly requests idiomatic Scala and standard-library usage; the agent produced a large custom implementation (including JSON ADT, functor/monad simulation) that is not obviously mandated by the task instruction excerpt.

diagnoses.prediction_id: wml-2-full-source inventory before translation (read-all → enumerate → map)

diagnoses.evidence: First file view shows `/root/Tokenizer.py` truncated after line ~94; second view covers 220–581 but is also truncated in the middle with `...[truncated]` around the TokenRegistry section. Implementation begins before any evidence of a complete read of all lines (no full `view_range` to cover missing middle).

diagnoses.description: Stopping verification after achieving compilation can miss semantic mismatches, API completeness gaps, and edge-case handling differences.
diagnoses.evidence: Tool calls show repeated `scalac` compilation until success; no evidence of executing Scala code, running sample tokenizations, or comparing to Python behavior. Agent message claims functional completeness but provides no test evidence.

diagnoses.evidence: Agent message and compilation log show added components: `JsonValue` ADT, pretty rendering, `TokenFunctor`/`TokenMonad`, registry/containers; task requirement only mandates presence of specific named classes/functions. diagnoses.prediction_id: wml-1-Dependency-scope binding for lockfile scans (prod vs dev/test; lockfile-only vs filesystem context)
diagnoses.description: When using a vulnerability scanner on dependency lockfiles, default flags/target mode can change the dependency scope (e.g., include dev/test deps, include transitive graphs differently, or analyze filesystem context). This yields a superset/different set of findings versus an evaluation ground truth built on a specific scope policy.

locations.section: Offline Scanning Workflow / Step 2: Construct Trivy Command

diagnoses.evidence: Verifier: generated CSV had 5 more items than expected ("Left contains 5 more items"). Trajectory: Trivy emitted "Suppressing dependencies for development and testing. To display them, try the '--include-dev-deps' flag." Yet output still contained many findings (24) and included multiple packages/versions; mismatch indicates scan scope differed from the ground truth's expected vulnerability set. No step binds scope to match expected (e.g., production-only vs include-dev, lockfile-only parsing mode, or npm-specific mode).

diagnoses.prediction_id: wml-2-Canonical vulnerability record identity & deterministic selection across multiple advisories
diagnoses.description: A package/version may have multiple vulnerabilities; scanners may emit multiple IDs (CVE vs vendor advisory IDs), multiple fixed versions, and multiple source records. If the reporting pipeline de-duplicates or selects records without a stable identity rule, it can substitute one advisory for another or report the wrong fixed version/CVSS for the same package/version.

locations.section: Field Mapping from JSON to CSV / Severity-Based Filtering

diagnoses.evidence: Verifier diff shows for key ('tar','6.1.11') the generated row had CVE_ID 'CVE-2026-73566' with CVSS_Score 7.5 and Fixed_Version 7.5.21, but expected 'CVE-2026-23745' with CVSS 8.2 and Fixed_Version 7.5.3. This indicates the pipeline reported a different advisory record for the same package/version than the ground truth expected. The script also deduplicates by (pkg, ver, cve) but does not implement a canonicalization/preference rule among multiple advisories for the same package/version.

diagnoses.prediction_id: wml-3-CVSS source/version priority binding & validation against selected advisory
diagnoses.description: Different data sources (NVD/GHSA/RedHat) can report different CVSS scores for the same CVE. If the extraction policy differs from the evaluator’s expected priority/version, reported scores will mismatch even if the right CVE is selected.
diagnoses.evidence: Verifier shows for ('tar','6.1.11') expected CVSS_Score 8.2 whereas generated CSV shows different CVSS values for tar HIGH (example head shows tar CVE-2026-23745 HIGH had 6.1). The script uses `SOURCE_PRIORITY=['nvd','ghsa','redhat']` and V3 then V2 fallback, but the earlier sample vulnerability showed CVSS keys only ['ghsa','redhat'], indicating NVD may be absent for some; expected may prefer a different source or metric mapping for those cases.

diagnoses.prediction_id: wml-4-Two-stage verification: schema + semantic record-set reconciliation
diagnoses.description: Pipelines that verify only formatting (headers, required fields, severity filter) can still be wrong on record selection, ID choice, and score/fix correctness. A missing verification step allows silent semantic drift.
diagnoses.evidence: Trajectory includes a validation script that checks column presence and severity counts, but no step checks for duplicates beyond (pkg,ver,cve) or reconciles the finding set. Verifier failure is precisely a content mismatch (extra rows and differing tar record), which would not be caught by the agent’s verification.
